findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the scoped fingerprint as NET-NEW per-path git-blob-sha resolution (a new helper that hashes the blob sha of each file_impact path via git, with defined empty/read-error/off-git fallback), rather than a reuse of BankStamps/resolve_bank_stamps — which only carry a plan-text material_fingerprint and a whole-tree sha, neither of which is per-path blob content.
evidence: BankStamps dataclass fields (completion_banking.py:328-337): ticket_id, material_fingerprint, tree_sha — no blob-sha field
material_fingerprint (pass1.py:495-534) hashes material_basis (description/AC/file_impact/decomposition) via sha256 of a JSON blob — plan text, not file contents
resolve_bank_stamps (completion_banking.py:340) resolves material fingerprint + whole-tree sha only
plan quote: 'the scoped fingerprint reuses BankStamps/resolve_bank_stamps (:358-392) narrowed to blobs under the ticket's file_impact paths'
findings.finding: The cross-run cache's scoped-fingerprint invalidation is described as 'reusing BankStamps/resolve_bank_stamps narrowed to blobs under file_impact paths' and 'resolving to blob shas through BankStamps/resolve_bank_stamps', but neither seam resolves file-blob content: BankStamps has only {ticket_id, material_fingerprint, tree_sha}, and material_fingerprint hashes the ticket's PLAN TEXT (description/AC/file_impact declarations/decomposition), not the bytes of files under those paths. The per-path blob-sha fingerprint is net-new code, not a reuse.
scenarios: Implementer follows the plan literally, tries to narrow BankStamps to per-path blobs, finds no such capability and must invent git blob-sha resolution — an unplanned mechanism whose atomicity/error paths are unspecified
findings.suggested_fix: Add a small helper (e.g. resolve_file_impact_blobs(paths, repo_root)) that runs `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` (or ls-tree) per file_impact path, sorts and hashes the {path: blob_sha} map, and defines the fallback to whole-tree sha for empty/unreadable paths; store this scoped hash in the verdict cache entry alongside the criterion-text hash.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the scoped fingerprint keys on ACTUAL file-content (per-path blob sha), not the plan-text material_fingerprint, so an in-scope code edit invalidates the cached PASS; add a RED test where a file under file_impact changes (ticket text unchanged) and the cached PASS is correctly invalidated.
evidence: material_fingerprint changes only on ticket material-text edits (pass1.py:502-508: description/AC/file_impact declarations/decomposition), NOT on file-content changes
AC3: 'invalidation on fingerprint or text change is RED->GREEN; an unrelated commit outside file_impact does NOT invalidate'
plan explicitly rejects whole-tree sha because 'any unrelated commit rotates it' — leaving only a per-path blob signal to detect in-scope content edits, which the cited seams do not compute
findings.finding: AC3 requires 'an unrelated commit outside file_impact does NOT invalidate' AND 'invalidation on fingerprint or text change is RED->GREEN', but if the design degrades to the actual material_fingerprint (which does NOT reflect file-content edits), a code edit UNDER file_impact that changes a criterion's truth without touching the ticket text would fail to invalidate the cached PASS — crediting a stale/incorrect PASS. The plan does not reconcile which signal detects an in-scope content edit.
scenarios: A criterion previously PASSed; a later commit edits a file under file_impact so the criterion is now UNMET, but the ticket text is unchanged; on re-verify the stale PASS is seeded and credited, and merge_finalizer bypass makes it un-downgradable — an incorrect certified close

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how `seeded: true` records are handled in `assemble_deterministic_verdict` (the second bank consumer, deterministic-fallback path), co-locating the seeded decision rule with that renderer — not only with `merge_finalizer_with_bank`.
evidence: Plan step 3 scopes the seeded bypass only to merge_finalizer_with_bank: 'records flagged seeded: true bypass finalizer judgment — an echo of a seeded record ... is replaced by the bank's validated-PASS record'

assemble_deterministic_verdict (completion_verdict_assembly.py:71-83) reads `met = bool(entry.get('met'))` as-is with no seeded handling — it is a second, independent bank consumer used 'when the LLM finalizer fails twice' (docstring :55)

Precedent ticket 1d71 enumerated BOTH bank-rendering seams together ('both placeholder branches', 'Deterministic assembly and both placeholder branches carry the marker') — the pattern here is to change consumers together
findings.finding: The `seeded: true` marker's decision rule (bypass finalizer judgment, credit the banked record verbatim) is co-located with only ONE of the two bank-consuming verdict renderers: the plan scopes the change to `merge_finalizer_with_bank`, but `assemble_deterministic_verdict` (completion_verdict_assembly.py:44) — the deterministic fallback that renders a verdict directly from bank entries when the LLM finalizer fails twice — also reads banked `met` and is never mentioned; the seeded protocol is not co-located with that schema consumer.
findings.location: Plan step 3 / AC line 3 ('the merge path credits seeded records verbatim'); src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_verdict_assembly.py:44 (assemble_deterministic_verdict) vs :147 (merge_finalizer_with_bank)
scenarios: A re-verify seeds cached PASS records, the LLM finalizer fails twice, and the deterministic fallback renders the verdict — the plan does not specify that seeded PASS entries are credited/annotated there (they happen to carry met=true, but the seeded semantics and any 'credited-from-cache' provenance are unspecified for this path)
findings.suggested_fix: Add to step 3 that assemble_deterministic_verdict credits seeded entries verbatim (and carries their seeded/credited provenance) exactly as the merge path does, with a RED test on the finalizer-fails-twice branch.

The 1d71 precedent (comment: 'merge_finalizer_with_bank re-stamps from the bank over model echoes ... finalizer prompt updated'; description: 'stamp = enforcement, prompt = text alignment') paired the code re-stamp WITH a finalizer-prompt update

The plan does not state whether seeded criteria are excluded from the finalizer's payload (the manifest omission at completion_recovery.py:540 targets the PRIMARY run, not the finalizer), leaving open whether the finalizer sees criteria it cannot influence
findings.finding: The plan enforces the seeded-record bypass purely in code (the merge restamp) but never aligns the finalizer PROMPT (completion_verifier_finalizer.md) nor states whether the finalizer's input payload still contains the seeded criteria; if the finalizer is still shown seeded criteria while its judgment on them is silently overridden, that is an instruction-locality / pink-elephant mismatch between prompt and enforcement.
scenarios: The finalizer is handed the full criteria list including seeded ones, judges a seeded criterion met=false, and the merge silently overrides it — the finalizer's prompt still instructs it to judge those criteria, so its instructions contradict the enforced behavior
